Pole Position: Earn Your Own Win
His teammate let him through for the win. Now he has to decide what to thank him for.
One correct team order, two opposite readings of it. A rookie wants his own name on his own win; his senior teammate wants to protect him, and himself.

In a fictional world racing series, veteran Luca Ferri lets rookie teammate Jack Whitaker past on worn tires, and Jack takes his first win. The call was right. The story Luca told afterward made Jack look like a project. You decide how Jack takes his name back — in the data, in the garage, and across a breakfast table with no lap times.
The race engineer who made the call — and has the full, unedited radio on a drive in your pocket.
If nobody acts, Jack's first win becomes a gift in everyone's memory, and Luca becomes the man who gave it.
